correctness.rationale: The Li–Tang all-index bound and recurrence use the same vectors, weights, signs and nonnegative m as the frozen theorem. In the coefficient identity theta(0)=1 and xi=q+O(q²), so at q and q² the coordinates are a=y_{m,1} and b=12y_{m,1}+y_{m,2}. The h=12 term cancels, giving D_m=−Lambda^m_{2,1}. I recomputed both relevant columns via coefficients of theta xi^i at q³ and q⁶, and the fifteen exterior-square weights: the leading pair (2,1) has value 3 with Delta=395433=9·43937 and unit −1; every other pair has weight at least 4, with three zero minors. The next exterior-square iteration therefore has its unique least valuation 2m+9, while other terms have valuation at least 2m+10 by the all-index bound. The positive base minor 698368·3⁷ has unit 1; this gives the claimed alternating negative-sign determinant law and exact valuations. Li–Tang Theorem 1.2(ii) supplies existence at m+5 for all n, with n=0 trivial. Eliminating any integer multiplier from n=1 and n=2 at modulus 3^(m+6), and using Theorem 1.1 on the lower-level coefficients, would force D_m divisible by 3^(2m+8), a contradiction. In my own bounded reproduction (`/tmp/opencode/frozen-review-repro.py partition`), counting directly by odd part multiplicities and k choices of tag for multiplicity k replicated determinant valuations 7,9,11,13 and units 2,1,2,1 at depths 0–3, as well as both claimed congruence instances at each depth. I inspected but did not run the frozen checker. RESULT.md line 51 has a harmless u_3(0) typo for nu_3(0), already defined on line 21. Infinite-depth validation relies on the cited all-index bound and the exact induction, not on these examples.
